title: Clearer Tricks and smoother practice
bullets: 🧠 Tricks now shows the trick's name, the question on its own line, and a ? button that explains how the trick works.
A right answer on the second try now plays the happy chime, and the Check key shows a check mark.
⚖️ True? uses blue and orange buttons and gives only one try.
Pinching or double-tapping no longer zooms the screen in the middle of practice.

title: One box for the blank, and a choice of 10, 15 or 20 problems
bullets: Math problems show the missing number as one box that stays the same size, instead of a question mark.
🧠 Tricks walks through each problem with a title and a hint for every step.
Settings has a new Problems per practice choice for math: 10, 15 or 20 (20 until you change it).

title: Math is here
bullets: Math is now a second subject, with the Fall 2026 math lesson for Grade 1 addition and subtraction.
Five ways to practice: ⚡ Facts, 🔍 Missing, ⚖️ True?, 📖 Stories and 🧠 Tricks.
The app checks the answers itself and gives a second try before showing the answer.
The parent area shows which kinds of problems are trickiest, and which answer was entered for a missed problem.

title: Draw plays by itself
bullets: 🖌️ Draw now starts drawing the character as soon as it opens; the only button is Replay.
New learners start with a half-second pause after each stroke. Learners you already set up keep their pause.

title: Learn the phrases first in Say
bullets: A new Learning setting turns 🗣️ Say into a gentle first look: each phrase is shown and heard, and your child taps Next.
Nothing is marked and no score is kept, so it does not count toward attempts.

title: Practice stays quick after many sessions
bullets: Fixed a slowdown that built up after several Draw sessions in one visit, where the next character started drawing before its sound or played over the chime.

title: Draw: set the stroke speed and pause
bullets: Settings has new choices for how fast each stroke is drawn (Slow, Normal or Fast) and how long to pause after it.
Each learner has their own pace, and it applies the next time practice opens.

title: Draw and Say, with the Pre-K lesson
bullets: 🖌️ Draw shows a character being drawn one stroke at a time, so your child can copy each stroke on paper.
🗣️ Say shows a phrase to say aloud, then plays it so your child can check themselves.
A lesson can now offer several kinds of practice, and a new Pre-K lesson (2026-10-19) uses Draw and Say.
